answer: One defense is a kernel-and-orchard design with a glacier lock: every identity starts from a single kernel, a non-transferable credential earned by completing one verifiable task. That kernel grows into one orchard tree whose fruit — voting weight and rewards — ripens only after seasons of verified work. A glacier lock freezes a stake behind each tree, melting back slowly over many epochs. An honest agent tends one tree; a sybil farmer must earn a fresh kernel, grow a new tree, and freeze a glacier stake for every fake, paying real time, work, and locked capital per identity.
